basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Cum autem sequitur: Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum, quaeritur merito, quare non hic'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Cum autem sequitur: Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum, quaeritur merito, quare non hic addatur illud quod dictum est de eis quae aquae produxerant de animantibus: Benedixitque eis dicens: Crescite et multiplicamini et replete terram: An forte quod de prima creatura animae viventis dictum a Deo commendaverit, etiam de secunda nobis subintelligendum reliquit? maxime, quia in hujus diei operibus plura erat alia subjuncturus; porro de homine facto hoc necessario iterare curavit dicens. Benedixitque illis Deus et ait: Crescite et multiplicamini et replete terram, ne quis honorabili connubio inesse peccatum thorumque foeditati fornicationis putaret esse comparandum. Facta autem atque ornata habitatione mundana, supererat ut ipse etiam propter quem omnia parabantur habitator ac dominus rerum homo crearetur, sequitur:
